forecasts.question: Will AGI be developed before 1 January 2030?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 21%. No formal AGI declaration. June 2026 news: Anthropic confidentially filed for IPO (1 Jun); Microsoft's Build 2026 unveiled MAI-Code-1-Flash and Suleyman's pitch for Microsoft as a 4th frontier lab. Air Street's State of AI (May 2026) notes continued capability gains but no lab is publicly calling AGI achieved. Amodei remains bullish (~2027) and Hassabis cautious.
forecasts.base_rate: Resolution requires a credible public AGI claim from a major lab OR 3+ leading researchers stating AGI achieved, before 1 Jan 2030 (~3.5 yrs out). Reference class of 'transformational tech' announcements suggests labs typically wait until capability is unambiguous; definitional disputes raise the bar.

factors_up.factor: Amodei (Anthropic) maintaining ~2027 AGI timeline; competitive pressure among 6+ frontier-tier labs
Capability gains continuing (Stanford AI Index 2026; 30pp jump on Humanity's Last Exam in a year)
AI-automating-AI feedback loops increasingly cited by lab leaders

factors_down.factor: No major lab has issued any formal AGI claim as of June 2026
Definitional ambiguity raises bar for the '3+ senior researchers' clause
Hassabis (DeepMind) remains cautious on autonomous self-improvement / scientific creativity

key_uncertainties: Whether internal capability translates to public AGI declarations before 2030
Whether IPO pressure on OpenAI/Anthropic incentivises or deters such claims
Pace of AI-automating-AI loops in 2027-2029
update_triggers: Formal AGI claim from a frontier lab
Public statement by 2+ senior researchers at OpenAI/Anthropic/DeepMind that AGI is achieved
Major step-change on AGI-relevant evals (METR, HLE, ARC-AGI v3)

forecasts.question: Will economic consultancy lose ≥33% value/jobs by end 2030 due to AI?
forecasts.key_change: Down 3pp to 24%. Fresh 2026 evidence is net negative for resolution: BCG hired ~1,000 new AI-services staff; McKinsey is planning 12% headcount growth in 2026; Bain says AI/tech-enabled work is ~30% of revenue, projected to 50%. AI is a net job creator at Big 3 today. Entry-level squeeze is real but offset by AI specialist hiring; revenue trajectory is up, not down.
forecasts.base_rate: Resolution requires industry-wide ≥33% decline in revenue OR employment vs 2024 baseline by end-2030, attributed primarily to AI by 2+ credible analyses. Sector contraction of that magnitude in a 6-yr window is historically rare absent broader recession.

factors_up.factor: Generative AI continues to compress entry-level analyst work and pricing models
Pressure on hourly/headcount-billing models as AI productivity becomes visible to clients
Possibility of a 2027-2029 recession compounding AI-driven restructuring

factors_down.factor: Big 3 currently growing on AI-related demand: BCG ~$3.6B AI revenue (25% of 2025 total), expecting ~40% by 2026
Net hiring still positive: McKinsey +12% planned 2026; BCG +1,000 AI staff
Resolution requires '2+ credible analyses attributing primarily to AI' — high evidentiary bar

key_uncertainties: Whether 2027-2030 sees a structural pricing collapse offsetting AI revenue growth
Definition of 'consultancy' (Big 3 strategy vs. broader management/IT consulting)
Macro backdrop: recession vs. soft landing
update_triggers: Major firm announcing >10% headcount cuts citing AI
Industry revenue contraction reported by Source Global / Kennedy / ALM
Shift from time-and-materials to value-based pricing across Big 3

forecasts.question: Will Labour be largest party at next UK General Election?
forecasts.key_change: Down 1pp to 4%. Polling deteriorated further: Labour 18-19% vs Reform 27% (YouGov/PollCheck early June). PLMR seat model projects Labour ~86 seats — collapse from 412. Local elections (7 May 2026) saw Labour lose 38 councils. Reform's lead is durable across pollsters.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: governing parties with sub-25% poll share ~3.5 yrs from an election rarely recover to first-place finishes. Historic UK base rate for an incumbent recovering this far from this deep a hole is in single digits.

factors_up.factor: Election still ~3 yrs away; Reform vote efficiency uncertain; FPTP can split anti-Labour vote
Possible Conservative-Reform split keeps Labour as plurality on similar share
Macro recovery / shift in cost of living could rebuild Labour support

factors_down.factor: Labour now level/behind Conservatives in some polls, well behind Reform
PLMR seat model: ~86 Labour seats — implies catastrophic loss
May 2026 local election results consistent with national polls; no leadership rebound visible

key_uncertainties: Whether Reform consolidates or fractures the right-of-centre vote by 2029
Whether Starmer remains Labour leader through to the GE
Macroeconomic trajectory 2027-2029
update_triggers: Labour returning to >25% in 7-poll average
Reform-Conservative formal pact or split
Change in Labour leadership

forecasts.question: Will AGI be developed before 1 January 2035?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 78%. ~8.5 yrs to deadline gives ample room for either definitional convergence or unambiguous capability. Insider survey medians cluster in late-2020s to early-2030s; aimultiple's 2026 aggregation of ~9,800 predictions concentrates by 2035. No specific new June signal materially shifts this.
forecasts.base_rate: Aggregated forecaster surveys (Metaculus, aimultiple's 9,800-prediction analysis, AI Insider surveys) put median AGI before 2035 at 60-80%. Lab leaders (Amodei, Hassabis, Altman) all project pre-2035 with varying confidence.

factors_up.factor: Multiple frontier labs predicting AGI before 2030 with 8+ yrs of buffer
Compute/algorithm trajectory remains exponential; AI-automating-AI compounding
Resolution standard (lab announcement OR 3+ researchers) is fairly soft over 9 yrs

factors_down.factor: Unknown unknowns / capability plateaus (e.g., reasoning, long-horizon agency)
Definitional disputes could persist even with strong capability
Possible regulatory or compute shock 2027-2032

key_uncertainties: Whether scaling continues or hits a wall in 2027-2030
Whether 'AGI' as a term retains social meaning by 2035
Geopolitical disruption to compute supply chains
update_triggers: Major capability plateau on frontier benchmarks for >12 months
Formal AGI claim from a major lab
Compute/regulatory shock disrupting frontier training

forecasts.question: Will China initiate a military blockade or invasion of Taiwan before 1 January 2030?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 8%. US intelligence (Mar 2026) assesses no fixed PLA timeline; amphibious assault unlikely by 2027. PLA continues gray-zone (90+ ship deployments late 2025) but not a >72hr blockade. Taiwan passed $25B defence supplemental. Status quo deterrence holding.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: PRC has never executed a >72hr blockade or assault on Taiwan proper. Major-power initiated wars in any given ~3.5 yr window have low base rate (~5-10%) absent acute trigger.

factors_up.factor: Continued PLA exercises simulating blockade ops
Xi's domestic political timeline; 2027 PLA modernisation milestone
Risk of accidental escalation from gray-zone activity

factors_down.factor: US IC assessment: no fixed timeline, amphibious assault unlikely by 2027
Massive economic cost to China; semiconductor dependency cuts both ways
Gray-zone coercion is PRC's preferred lever — substitutes for kinetic action

key_uncertainties: Whether a Taiwan independence-leaning move triggers escalation
US political posture / Trump administration response to a crisis
PLA confidence in joint-force readiness by 2027-2028
update_triggers: PLA mobilisation beyond exercise patterns
Taiwan referendum or formal independence move
PRC ASBM/anti-access deployments to forward bases

forecasts.question: Will UK annual CPI inflation fall below 2.0% for at least one month before 1 January 2027?
forecasts.key_change: Up 1pp to 5%. ONS April 2026 CPI: 2.8% (vs 3.3% March, 3.0% Feb). Trend is downward but still 80bp above target, with only 7-8 monthly prints remaining before Jan 2027 deadline. Energy base effects and services inflation remain sticky; BoE projects CPI to slow to ~2% only in late 2027.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: UK CPI annual rate has been ≥2.0% every month since mid-2021. A drop from 2.8% to <2.0% in <6 months requires ~80bp of disinflation — historically requires sustained negative output gap or commodity shock.

factors_up.factor: Downward trend in CPI (3.3% → 2.8%) over March-April 2026
Possible energy/utility base effects in autumn 2026
Weak demand from cooling labour market

factors_down.factor: Services inflation still well above 2%; wage growth ~5%
BoE central projection has CPI back to 2% only in 2027
Only 7-8 monthly prints remaining before Jan 2027 deadline

key_uncertainties: Magnitude of energy base effects Q4 2026
Whether services inflation breaks sharply lower
Sterling and commodity price moves
update_triggers: May 2026 CPI print (due ~18 June) showing further decline
Sharp drop in Brent/UK natural gas prices
Services CPI breaking below 3.5%

forecasts.question: Will Spider-Man: Brand New Day gross over $1.5B worldwide by 31 December 2026?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 78%. Releases 31 July 2026. Trailer 1 hit 1.1B views in 4 days (record); Trailer 2 (~2:36) attached to Masters of the Universe (5 Jun). Polymarket: ~54.5% to be 2026's top domestic earner. Strong tracking; main risks are execution and front-loaded box office in soft global theatrical environment.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: prior MCU Spider-Man films opened to massive WW grosses (No Way Home: $1.92B; Far From Home: $1.13B). With Holland's return and MCU reset narrative, $1.5B is achievable but not guaranteed in current theatrical climate.

factors_up.factor: Record-shattering trailer engagement (1.1B views/4 days)
Tom Holland return + post-Doomsday narrative momentum
Light competition in late summer 2026 window

factors_down.factor: Global theatrical market still ~15-20% below 2019 levels
China access remains uncertain for major MCU releases
Execution risk: critical reception unknown

key_uncertainties: China release status and gross
Critical reception and word-of-mouth
Avengers: Doomsday opening (May 2026) cannibalisation
update_triggers: Opening weekend gross
Confirmed China release
Rotten Tomatoes score at release

forecasts.question: Will OpenAI and Anthropic have a combined ARR exceeding $70B by 31 December 2026?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 99%. Reporting in May/June 2026: Anthropic ~$45B ARR, OpenAI ~$33B ARR — combined ~$78B already above the $70B threshold. Q4 2026 ARR almost certain to be higher absent revenue collapse. OpenAI CRO memo disputes Anthropic by ~$8B; even at the low end the combined figure clears $70B.
forecasts.base_rate: Resolution requires 'most recent credible reporting' of Q4 2026 ARR to sum to >$70B. Combined figure is already above threshold mid-2026 with ARR growth >5% per month.

factors_up.factor: Combined ARR already ~$78B per credible reporting (May 2026)
Both companies still growing ARR materially month-on-month
Enterprise contracts (esp. Anthropic, 80% enterprise) provide stickiness

factors_down.factor: OpenAI CRO disputes Anthropic ARR by ~$8B — definitional risk
Possible Q3-Q4 enterprise spending pullback
Reporting methodology disputes could create ambiguity

key_uncertainties: How aggressively each company reports inference vs subscription ARR
Whether a Q4 2026 macro slowdown hits enterprise AI spend
Resolution sensitivity to which 'credible source' is used
update_triggers: Either company reports flat/declining ARR
Formal Q4 2026 disclosure
Audited financials showing lower-than-claimed run rates

forecasts.question: Will UK average annual real GDP growth exceed 1.5% across the 2030s (2030-2039)?
forecasts.key_change: Down 1pp to 35%. OBR March 2026 EFO has growth averaging 1.6% over the rest of its forecast window (through 2030-31), but with productivity headwinds and debt at 95% of GDP into early 2030s, the medium-term consensus is closer to 1.4-1.5%. AI productivity tailwind is the major upside not yet in forecaster models.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: UK 10-year real GDP growth has exceeded 1.5% in roughly half of post-1970 decades. 2010s averaged ~1.9%, 2020s tracking ~1.3% so far. OBR/IMF/OECD all cluster mid-term forecasts at ~1.3-1.6%.

factors_up.factor: AI-driven productivity upside not yet in mainstream forecasts
OBR central forecast averages 1.6% through 2030-31
Possible immigration / planning reform tailwinds

factors_down.factor: Productivity growth structurally weak post-2008; OBR briefing paper 9 highlights downside
Public debt ~95% of GDP constrains fiscal space
Demographic drag accelerating in late 2020s

key_uncertainties: Whether AI translates to GDP-level productivity gains by 2030s
Trade / geopolitical disruption trajectory
Whether next government implements supply-side reforms
update_triggers: OBR multi-decade outlook update
Significant policy package (planning, immigration, AI infra)
Productivity data inflection
